key_insight: Data-informed random features provide a compact function dictionary for learning continuous-time nonlinear dynamics through Koopman generator approximations.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports efficient forecasting and system analysis while retaining the interpretable linear-operator structure of the Koopman framework.
method: Approximate the Koopman generator using Galerkin methods such as gEDMD.
Establish convergence of the approximated vector field and resulting trajectories.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments demonstrate accurate forecasting and system analysis, with faster computation than iterative optimization; the abstract gives no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: gEDMD does not generally preserve exponential boundedness, so long-term growth behavior requires separate verification.
paper_title: Data-driven Random-feature Approximation of Koopman Generators of Nonlinear Continuous-time Systems
